name: Vinci SA
executive_summary:
Vinci SA is a diversified global infrastructure group spanning concessions (airports, motorways), energy solutions (Vinci Energies, Cobra IS) and construction, with roughly 59% of 2025 revenue generated outside France. The quantitative screen rates the name a strong buy on cheapness (P/E 13.7, P/B 2.1), quality (ROE 15.4%), dividend yield (4.2%) and cash generation, passing ten of twenty-two models across five factor families. FY 2025 primary filings show record free cash flow of €7.0 billion, net financial debt at 1.4× EBITDA and a proposed dividend of €5.00 per share, supporting a value-plus-income case. The central debate is whether modest reported earnings growth (+0.8% net income, dampened by a French exceptional tax charge) and cyclical/geopolitical headwinds (Middle East disruption at Gatwick, weak French autoroute traffic) are already priced in, or whether the record €74.9 billion order book and energy-transition backlog justify further re-rating. No formal interim (half-year) filing is present in the source pack; Q1 2026 trading data is available but classified as “other” rather than interim.

---
investment_thesis:
For a value investor, Vinci offers a rare combination of screen-passing valuation, durable cash conversion and shareholder returns within European industrials. The screen’s strong-buy signal rests on ten passing models — including Graham Enterprising, FCF Yield, Neff PEGY, Quality Value, Dividend Growth, Magic Formula, Acquirer’s Multiple, Piotroski F-Score, Composite Value and Earnings Quality — with full data quality (20/20 metrics) and a composite score of 0.875 (sector-relative 0.805). Key metrics align with business fundamentals disclosed in the FY 2025 results release: P/E 13.7 versus diluted EPS of €8.65; dividend yield ~4.1–4.2% on a €5.00 proposed payout (58% payout ratio); and FCF of €7.0 billion on revenue of €74.6 billion.

Business quality supports the screen rather than contradicting it. Concessions generated €3.9 billion of segment free cash flow on resilient traffic (334 million airport passengers, +5.0%; autoroute traffic +0.9%). Energy Solutions grew revenue 8% with margin improvement to 7.6%, riding electrification, data-centre and sovereignty-driven demand. Construction EBIT margin reached 4.2% with record segment FCF of €1.4 billion after working-capital discipline. The Q1 2026 update confirms visibility: order intake +5% to €17.4 billion and a record order book of €74.9 billion (~15 months of activity), with 2026 guidance unchanged.

The value case is not purely statistical. Net financial debt fell €1.3 billion to €19.1 billion (1.4× EBITDA) despite €2.0 billion of share buybacks; liquidity stands at €15.5 billion net cash plus a €6.5 billion undrawn facility. Credit ratings were reaffirmed (S&P A−/A2 stable; Moody’s A3/P-2 stable). Portfolio optimisation (Zero.e renewables spin-out logic, ADP exchangeable bonds, India highway expansion, Fletcher Construction in New Zealand) adds optionality without undermining the core concession-and-contracting cash engine that the screen’s FCF and dividend models capture.

**Source hierarchy:** Figures below are drawn from primary filing body extracts unless noted. Yahoo (`financials_annual.json`) is cited only where the filing pack lacks detail.

### Annual results (FY 2025 — filed 5 February 2026)

| Metric | FY 2025 | FY 2024 | Change |
|--------|---------|---------|--------|
| Revenue | €74,599m | €71,623m | +4.2% |
| EBITDA | €13,507m | €12,689m | +6.4% (18.1% margin) |
| EBIT (ordinary) | €9,600m | — | +6.2% (12.8% margin) |
| Net income (parent) | €4,903m | €4,863m | +0.8% |
| EPS (diluted) | €8.65 | €8.43 | +2.6% |
| Free cash flow | €7,010m | €6,808m | +€202m |
| Net financial debt | €19.1bn | — | −€1.3bn vs Dec-24 |
| Net debt / EBITDA | 1.4× | — | — |

**Excluding the French exceptional tax contribution** (€449m hit to net income; €425m to FCF), reported net income would have risen ~10% to €5,352m (EPS €9.44, +12%) and FCF ~€7,435m (+9%). This tax drag is a material headwind to headline earnings comparability and featured in sell-side commentary during the period.

Segment highlights (FY 2025 filing):
- **Concessions:** Revenue €12.0bn (+5%); EBITDA >€8.0bn; FCF €3.9bn (+€336m). Airports FCF record €1.2bn.
- **Energy Solutions:** Revenue €30.0bn (+8%); EBIT margin 7.6%; FCF €1.2bn after €1.1bn renewable capex at Cobra IS (segment FCF negative €365m).
- **Construction:** Revenue €33.0bn (+1%); EBIT margin >4%; record FCF €1.4bn.

Balance-sheet and capital allocation (FY 2025 filing): long-term gross debt €34.6bn; average maturity 5.5 years; average cost 4.4%. Share buybacks of €2.0bn (16.6m shares); proposed dividend €5.00 (+5.3%). 2026 guidance: further revenue, operating earnings and net income growth; initial FCF estimate ~€6.0bn (assuming similar Zero.e capex).

**Yahoo cross-check (`financials_annual.json`, fallback):** Total revenue €75,702m and net income €4,903m for 2025 align closely with the filing on earnings; Yahoo reports FCF €8,013m and net debt €17,589m — higher FCF and lower net debt than the filing’s €7,010m and €19.1bn, likely reflecting definitional differences (e.g. IFRS 16 lease treatment; the filing explicitly excludes lease liabilities from net financial debt). Non-current pension obligations per Yahoo: €1,169m (2025). Goodwill and intangibles total €60.4bn, yielding negative tangible book value — a screen blind spot for asset-heavy concessionaires.

### Multi-year trend (Yahoo fallback for historical context only)

Revenue has grown from €62.5bn (2022) to €75.7bn (2025 per Yahoo); net income from €4.26bn to €4.90bn; FCF from €5.89bn to €8.01bn (Yahoo). Operating margins have expanded gradually. Interest expense rose to €1.51bn in 2025 (from €810m in 2022), consistent with higher rates and acquisition-led debt, partially offset by lower average funding cost (4.4% vs 4.9%).

risks_and_flags:
**Tax and regulatory (France):** The FY 2025 filing documents an exceptional contribution on large-company profits (€449m net income impact) and notes the higher French corporate income tax rate (~36%) applies through 2026. BofA downgraded Vinci to Underperform citing French tax risks (*“Vinci stock downgraded to Underperform by BofA on French tax risks”*, 13 January 2026). Cofiroute toll-indexation adjustments and regional development tax offsets add regulatory complexity.

**Geopolitical and cyclical:** Q1 2026 filing language highlights Middle East conflict disrupting London Gatwick (−3.6% passengers Q1), China–Japan tensions affecting Kansai, and farmers’ blockades hitting French autoroute traffic. H1 2026 airport traffic was “stable” with Q2 geopolitical decline (*“VINCI Airports – Traffic as of June 30, 2026”*, 16 July 2026). These are material for the concessions cash engine despite geographic diversification.

**Leverage and balance sheet:** Net financial debt of €19.1–19.8bn (1.4× EBITDA) is manageable and rating-agency affirmed, but total debt per Yahoo is €37.7bn with heavy intangible assets (goodwill €20.2bn). Tangible book value is deeply negative (−€29.7bn per Yahoo), limiting asset-based downside protection.

**Capex and FCF volatility:** Cobra IS/Zero.e renewable investments consumed €0.9bn in 2025 with negative segment FCF; 2026 group FCF guidance (~€6bn) is below 2025’s record €7.0bn. Construction revenue phasing caused Q1 declines; major-project concentration remains a margin and timing risk.

**M&A and portfolio execution:** Active deal pipeline (Fletcher Construction ~€630m revenue; Safeway India ~700 km; FM Conway, Edinburgh airport integrations) carries integration and approval risk. Portfolio reviews may lead to disposals or increased stakes — strategic uncertainty rather than distress.

**Governance transition:** Pierre Anjolras became CEO in May 2025; Thierry Mirville succeeds Christian Labeyrie as CFO from 1 June 2026 (*yfinance*, 4 June 2026). Xavier Huillard renewed as Chairman (April 2026 AGM). No going-concern qualification appears in available filing bodies; liquidity and covenant headroom appear ample (€15.5bn cash; undrawn €6.5bn facility to January 2031).

**Pension:** Non-current pension obligations ~€1.2bn (Yahoo 2025) — not flagged as acute in filings but worth monitoring alongside €8.4bn current provisions.

**Source gaps:** No half-year filing in index; no audited full annual report body (press release only); news manifest heavily contaminated by Dollar General (NYSE: DG) ticker collisions — company-specific risk monitoring is impaired.

research_rationale: Primary filings confirm the screen’s strong-buy pillars — cheap multiples, high ROE, rising dividend and record cash generation — but French tax drag, geopolitical concession sensitivity and the absence of a half-year filing in the source pack warrant accumulation rather than unqualified endorsement.
